header.text: The following passage describes how previous time periods influenced the Renaissance. Read the passage. Then follow the instructions below.

textContent.text: The Renaissance is known as a time of new ideas in art and learning. However, many of the movement's practices and beliefs came from the ancient past. That is why the word "Renaissance" means "rebirth."

Renaissance thinkers were familiar with the ideas of the Middle Ages, a period of time that began after the fall of the Roman Empire. During the Middle Ages, artists and writers in Europe usually focused on religious subjects, such as God and heaven.

But Renaissance thinkers wanted to study ideas from ancient Greece and Rome. Greek and Roman artists and writers usually focused on nonreligious subjects, such as people and nature. They used reason and scientific thinking in their work.
Renaissance artists and scholars combined themes from both periods to create new ideas and artwork.

contents.text: Historians have studied the Renaissance for centuries. Most historians agree that the Renaissance was a time of new art and learning. But they haven't always agreed on the importance of the Middle Ages or how the Middle Ages impacted the Renaissance.

header.text: Read the following summaries of two historians' views on the relationship between the Renaissance and the Middle Ages. Then follow the instructions below.

textContent.text: During the Middle Ages, it was like people were half-awake or dreaming underneath a veil. This veil was made of childish beliefs and misunderstandings that kept them from seeing the world clearly. But in Italy during the Renaissance, this veil began to disappear. People were able to learn about many subjects and create beautiful new art.
Adapted from Jacob Burckhardt and S. G. C. Middlemore, translator, The Civilization of the Renaissance in Italy. Copyright 1928 by George Allen & Unwin Ltd.

table.text: In the past, some historians saw the Middle Ages as a dark, gloomy time. But today, historians recognize the achievements of the Middle Ages. Artists, scholars, and inventors during the Middle Ages created works that helped to shape the Renaissance. Their ideas continue to influence our thinking, art, and culture today.

header.text: The following passage describes how previous time periods influenced the Renaissance. Read the passage. Then follow the instructions below.

textContent.text: The Renaissance is known as a time of new ideas in art and learning. However, many of the movement's practices and beliefs came from the ancient past. That is why the word "Renaissance" means "rebirth."

Renaissance thinkers were familiar with the ideas of the Middle Ages, a period of time that began after the fall of the Roman Empire. During the Middle Ages, artists and writers in Europe usually focused on religious subjects, such as God and heaven.

But Renaissance thinkers wanted to study ideas from ancient Greece and Rome. Greek and Roman artists and writers usually focused on nonreligious subjects, such as people and nature. They used reason and scientific thinking in their work.
Renaissance artists and scholars combined themes from both periods to create new ideas and artwork.

Renaissance thinkers were familiar with the ideas of the Middle Ages, a period of time that began after the fall of the Roman Empire. During the Middle Ages, artists and writers in Europe usually focused on religious subjects, such as God and heaven.

But Renaissance thinkers wanted to study ideas from ancient Greece and Rome. Greek and Roman artists and writers usually focused on nonreligious subjects, such as people and nature. They used reason and scientific thinking in their work.
Renaissance artists and scholars combined themes from both periods to create new ideas and artwork.

header.text: Read the following summaries of two historians' views on the relationship between the Renaissance and the Middle Ages. Then answer the question below.

contents.text: During the Middle Ages, it was like people were half-awake or dreaming underneath a veil. This veil was made of childish beliefs and misunderstandings that kept them from seeing the world clearly. But in Italy during the Renaissance, this veil began to disappear. People were able to learn about many subjects and create beautiful new art.

colHeaders.text: Events in Dante's journey through hell

elements.text: Dante meets two ancient Greek and Roman figures—a poet named Homer and a famous political leader named Julius Caesar. They are good men, but they are not allowed into heaven because they were alive before Christianity began.

pieces.text: Starting in the 1600s, a group of people in Europe began to think about the world in a different way. That new way of thinking led to a time period known as the
, often called the Enlightenment. Read the passage about the Enlightenment. Then follow the instructions below.

text.text: The "Age of Enlightenment" refers to a period of change in the way some educated men and women viewed the world and the role of humans within it. These educated men and women wanted people to use reason and experience, not traditional ideas, to make decisions and come to new conclusions. Enlightenment thinkers argued that humans were capable of using reason to make progress and improve people's lives. Their ideas led to new ways of thinking about topics such as government, religion, and people's rights.

text.text: The "Age of Enlightenment" refers to a period of change in the way some educated men and women viewed the world and the role of humans within it. These educated men and women wanted people to use reason and experience, not traditional ideas, to make decisions and come to new conclusions. Enlightenment thinkers argued that humans were capable of using reason to make progress and improve people's lives. Their ideas led to new ways of thinking about topics such as government, religion, and people's rights.

Starting in the 1600s, a group of people in Europe began to think about the world in a different way. That new way of thinking led to a time period known as the
, often called the Enlightenment. Read the passage about the Enlightenment. Then follow the instructions below.

text.text: The "Age of Enlightenment" refers to a period of change in the way some educated men and women viewed the world and the role of humans within it. These educated men and women wanted people to use reason and experience, not traditional ideas, to make decisions and come to new conclusions. Enlightenment thinkers argued that humans were capable of using reason to make progress and improve people's lives. Their ideas led to new ways of thinking about topics such as government, religion, and people's rights.

header.text: The black lines on the map represent trade routes in the 14th century. The following statements are true about these trade routes:

content.text: Some routes went across the sea.

explanationText.text: Some trade routes went across the sea. For example, Muslim merchants controlled trade routes in the Indian Ocean. They ferried goods to and from South and East Asia.

content.text: Some routes connected Europe to Africa and Asia.

explanationText.text: Trade routes reached from European cities such as Lisbon and Genoa all the way to Chinese cities in East Asia.

Some trade routes passed over land between Europe and Asia. Merchants would carry goods along sections of the route, and then hand them off to other traders, who would carry them forward. This work was often dangerous because people would rob trade caravans.

header.text: This statement is not true about trade routes:

content.text: None of the routes went through northern Africa.

pieces.text: Many trade routes
cross northern Africa. The map shows trade routes that connected inland African cities such as Timbuktu and Gao to cities on the Mediterranean Sea, such as Tunis and Alexandria.

content.text: It was next to the Atlantic Ocean.

explanationText.text: Portuguese sailors had easy access to the Atlantic Ocean. They were more familiar with wind patterns and ocean currents than people from many other European states. This knowledge later helped them sail far from home and back again successfully.

in sponsoring overseas expeditions. Other European countries, such as France and England, didn't play a large role in overseas exploration until later in the 1500s.

decided against making many overseas expeditions in the late 1400s. The Ming Dynasty ruled over parts of present-day China.

contents.text: While the Portuguese were working their way around the coast of Africa, other European countries, such as Spain, also wanted to trade in the Indian Ocean. But Portugal already controlled sea trade along the West African coast. In fact, the rulers of Spain had signed a treaty agreeing not to trade there.

Imagine you are the ruler of Spain. You are determined to trade in the Indian Ocean, but the Portuguese are blocking you from sending expeditions around Africa. What would be the best solution to this problem?

look for other routes to the Indian Ocean

After the cloth crisis, Queen Elizabeth I needed to find new sources of wealth for England. As part of her search for wealth, she sponsored a navigator named
to lead a voyage to the Americas. Drake later became the first English navigator to circumnavigate the world.

header.text: The map below shows the circumnavigation routes of Ferdinand Magellan and Sir Francis Drake. Look at the map. Then answer the question.

alternativeText.text: A world map. Ferdinand Magellan began his voyage in 1519, starting in Spain. Travelling southwest, he followed the western coast of Africa, crossed the narrowest part of the Atlantic Ocean, and then followed the eastern coast of South America. He rounded the tip of South America before continuing to the northwest across the Pacific Ocean. He passed through the Philippines while navigating through Southeast Asia, before travelling southwest through the Indian Ocean and around South Africa. From there, he travelled northwest, passing western Africa and returning to Spain in 1522.  Sir Francis Drake began his voyage in 1577, starting in England. At first, he followed almost the same route as Magellan, until he reached the tip of South America. From there, he travelled north, following the western coast of South America and stopping in Peru and Mexico. He continued until he reached present-day California, turned around, and began travelling southwest through the Pacific Ocean. He passed through the Philippines while navigating through Southeast Asia, and from there followed almost the same route as Magellan. He returned to England in 1580.

Then, in the mid-1500s, the English government began sending expeditions again. Read the passage about the events in England that created new interest in expeditions. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: In the middle of the 1500s, England's main source of wealth was trading English cloth in foreign markets. Thousands of people in England made their livings by producing or selling cloth, and the English government made money by taxing the sale of cloth. But in 1551, some foreign powers stopped allowing people to purchase English cloth. Many English people who worked in the cloth industry lost their jobs, and the government could not raise as much money.

pieces.text: These conditions created a national crisis. The Queen of England,
, needed to find new sources of wealth to address the crisis. Queen Elizabeth thought that sending expeditions to the Americas might be one way to help.

header.text: The map below shows the circumnavigation routes of Ferdinand Magellan and Sir Francis Drake. Look at the map. Then answer the question.

alternativeText.text: A world map. Ferdinand Magellan began his voyage in 1519, starting in Spain. Travelling southwest, he followed the western coast of Africa, crossed the narrowest part of the Atlantic Ocean, and then followed the eastern coast of South America. He rounded the tip of South America before continuing to the northwest across the Pacific Ocean. He passed through the Philippines while navigating through Southeast Asia, before travelling southwest through the Indian Ocean and around South Africa. From there, he travelled northwest, passing western Africa and returning to Spain in 1522.  Sir Francis Drake began his voyage in 1577, starting in England. At first, he followed almost the same route as Magellan, until he reached the tip of South America. From there, he travelled north, following the western coast of South America and stopping in Peru and Mexico. He continued until he reached present-day California, turned around, and began travelling southwest through the Pacific Ocean. He passed through the Philippines while navigating through Southeast Asia, and from there followed almost the same route as Magellan. He returned to England in 1580.

contents.text: In 1492, Christopher Columbus landed in the Americas. After he returned to Spain, the Spanish government sent more ships to the Americas and took control of large areas of land. Other European leaders saw Spain's success and sent their own ships to the Americas.

pieces.text: The arrows on the map below show where Europeans arrived in

alternativeText.text: The English arrived in several places along the east coast and in the north. Indigenous groups who already lived in or near those areas include the Cree, Iroquois, Shawnee, Cherokee and others. Russians arrived on the west coast where the Chumash people lived. The French arrived in central America, where Natches, Pawnee, Sioux, Assinboine and other groups lived. The Dutch arrived in the north east where the Iroquois lived. Spanish arrived in several locations in the south including locations where indigenous groups like Apache, Aztec, Maya, Chumash, and others lived. The Swedish arrived along the east coast near where the Shawnee and Iroquois lived.

contents.text: In 1492, Christopher Columbus landed in the Americas. After he returned to Spain, the Spanish government sent more ships to the Americas and took control of large areas of land. Other European leaders saw Spain's success and sent their own ships to the Americas.

pieces.text: The arrows on the map below show where Europeans arrived in

alternativeText.text: The English arrived in several places along the east coast and in the north. Indigenous groups who already lived in or near those areas include the Cree, Iroquois, Shawnee, Cherokee and others. Russians arrived on the west coast where the Chumash people lived. The French arrived in central America, where Natches, Pawnee, Sioux, Assinboine and other groups lived. The Dutch arrived in the north east where the Iroquois lived. Spanish arrived in several locations in the south including locations where indigenous groups like Apache, Aztec, Maya, Chumash, and others lived. The Swedish arrived along the east coast near where the Shawnee and Iroquois lived.

contents.text: In 1492, Christopher Columbus landed in the Americas. After he returned to Spain, the Spanish government sent more ships to the Americas and took control of large areas of land. Other European leaders saw Spain's success and sent their own ships to the Americas.

pieces.text: The arrows on the map below show where Europeans arrived in
between 1500 and 1800. Look at the map. Then follow the instructions below.

alternativeText.text: The English arrived in several places along the east coast and in the north. Indigenous groups who already lived in or near those areas include the Cree, Iroquois, Shawnee, Cherokee and others. Russians arrived on the west coast where the Chumash people lived. The French arrived in central America, where Natches, Pawnee, Sioux, Assinboine and other groups lived. The Dutch arrived in the north east where the Iroquois lived. Spanish arrived in several locations in the south including locations where indigenous groups like Apache, Aztec, Maya, Chumash, and others lived. The Swedish arrived along the east coast near where the Shawnee and Iroquois lived.

pieces.text: The Columbian Exchange started in

, when Europeans first began coming to the Americas in large numbers. As ships began to travel between the Americas and the rest of the world, they brought many new things with them that were part of the Columbian Exchange: plants, animals, people, and diseases.
